title: Two Non-Overlapping Blocks

concept.title: Best first block so far, plus the second block
body: You must choose a block of length `p` and a block of length `q` that do not overlap, in either order, with the largest total sum. First assume the `p`-block comes **before** the `q`-block. Walk with `i` as the end of the `q`-block. Keep `bestFirst`, the best sum of a `p`-block that ends at or before the start of the `q`-block, and combine it with the `q`-block ending at `i`.
Block sums come from prefix sums. Then swap the roles of `p` and `q` to cover the other order, and take the larger result. One pass, constant work per position.

statement: Given an array of `n` integers and two lengths `p` and `q` (with `p + q <= n`), choose a block of `p` consecutive elements and a block of `q` consecutive elements that do not share any position. The first block may be on either side of the second. Print the largest possible total sum of the chosen elements.
constraints: 1 <= p, q and p + q <= n

examples.note: Choose the block [9] of length 1 and the block [6 5] of length 2: 9 + 11 = 20.

hints: Build prefix sums so that any block sum is a difference of two entries.
Assume the p-block is first: while moving the end of the q-block, remember the best p-block that finishes before it starts.
Do the same with the roles swapped and take the larger result.

explanation: With prefix sums every block sum is O(1). For a fixed order, keep the best first block ending before the second block starts and combine it with the second block ending at each position. Try both orders.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

def best_total(pre, n, first, second):
    INF = 10**18
    bestFirst = -INF
    result = -INF
    for i in range(first + second, n + 1):
        bestFirst = max(bestFirst, pre[i - second] - pre[i - second - first])
        result = max(result, bestFirst + pre[i] - pre[i - second])
    return result

n, p, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

pre = [0] * (n + 1)
for i in range(n):
    pre[i + 1] = pre[i] + a[i]
print(max(best_total(pre, n, p, q), best_total(pre, n, q, p)))
